## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #14006: inline model referencing — support `@provider/model` mentions in prompts (SMALL priority, prompt parsing)

- **What**: Kilocode's composer now supports `@provider/model` mentions in user prompts (e.g. `@anthropic/claude-opus-4 explain this code`), which inserts an inline model reference token that is classified as text, NOT a file attachment. The orchestrator can pass the exact model to Agent Manager or the subagent tool, so a user can override the default model mid-conversation without opening Settings → Models or restarting the session with a different `--model` flag. The @ mention menu includes a "Model" entry that opens the shared model selector and inserts the reference. The token is inline text, so it survives draft restoration, copy-paste, and prompt templating. The seed-time classifier recognizes model references from the live model catalog, and attachment-sync reclassifies them on every catalog load so a model reference that looked like a file path before the catalog loaded (or after a catalog refresh) is correctly recognized.
- **Why**: Users switching between models mid-conversation (e.g. fast model for boilerplate, slow model for reasoning) have to change settings or restart the session, breaking flow. Inline model references let users override the model for a single turn (or multiple turns if the reference stays in the prompt) without leaving the composer. Alexi has no @ mention system — users must use `--model` flags (which require a new session or are ignored mid-session) or change `routing-config.json` (which affects all future sessions). A prompt-inline model override would let CLI users do the same: `ax chat -m "@anthropic/claude-opus-4 explain bubble sort"` runs that one message with opus instead of the session default.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14006 (feat(vscode): reference a model inline in the prompt with @)
- **Category**: command (CLI, prompt parsing, model override)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~2h. Alexi's orchestrator (src/core/orchestrator.ts, src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts) does not parse user messages for model overrides. Add a prompt-inline model override mechanism: before routing a turn, scan the user message text for `@<provider>/<model>` patterns (regex `@([a-z0-9-]+)/([a-z0-9-./]+)`), extract the model ID, validate it against the live model catalog (src/providers/modelCatalog.ts), and if found, override the route/model for that turn only (leaving the session's default model unchanged). Store the override in the turn context so the router (src/core/router.ts) uses it instead of the session default. Test by running `ax chat -m "test default model" -m "@anthropic/claude-opus-4 explain bubble sort"` and confirming the first turn uses the session default and the second turn uses opus (check logs or tool output for the selected model). Also test invalid model references (`@nonexistent/model`) and confirm they are ignored or surface a helpful error. Touches src/core/orchestrator.ts, src/core/streamingOrchestrator.ts, src/core/router.ts.

#### 2. Kilocode #14013: Kilo Swarm env flag — add runtime flag as alternative enable path (SMALL priority, board gating)

- **What**: Kilocode added `KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_SHARED_AGENT_BOARD` runtime flag (and the umbrella `KILO_EXPERIMENTAL`) as an alternative enable path to the existing `experimental.sharedAgentBoard` config key. The board is enabled when config is true OR flag is set (boolean OR, not XOR); an explicit config false does not disable the board when the flag is set. A `BoardEnabled.resolve` helper encodes the rule (config true or flag true) so every gate site shares one implementation. This allows users to enable Kilo Swarm via environment variable (useful for CI, Docker, or temporary testing) without editing `~/.alexi/config.json`.
- **Why**: The shared agent board (Kilo Swarm) was previously gated only by the `experimental.sharedAgentBoard` config key in `~/.alexi/config.json`. Users who wanted to test it in CI or a Docker container had to mount a custom config file or run a pre-flight `ax config set experimental.sharedAgentBoard true` step. Runtime flags are more convenient for temporary/environment-specific enablement and align with existing CLI conventions (`KILO_FLAGS`, `KILO_RETRIES`, `KILO_EXPERIMENTAL`). Alexi already gates the board tool on `experimental.sharedAgentBoard` config (src/tool/tools/board.ts, line 21: `if (!config.get('experimental.sharedAgentBoard')) return;`), but has no env flag path. Add the same env flag enable path so users can do `export KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_SHARED_AGENT_BOARD=1 && ax chat` or `KILO_EXPERIMENTAL=1 ax chat` instead of editing config.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14013 (feat(cli): enable shared agent board via experimental env flag)
- **Category**: config (board gating, environment variables)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~1h. Alexi's board tool registration (src/tool/tools/board.ts) checks only the config key. Add an env flag check: `process.env.KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_SHARED_AGENT_BOARD === '1'` or `process.env.KILO_EXPERIMENTAL === '1'` (the umbrella flag). Follow Kilocode's OR rule: board is enabled when config is true OR flag is set. Extract the check into a helper (e.g. `isBoardEnabled()` in src/tool/tools/board.ts or src/config/index.ts) so the rule lives in one place. Test by removing the config key (`ax config delete experimental.sharedAgentBoard`), setting `export KILO_EXPERIMENTAL_SHARED_AGENT_BOARD=1`, and running `ax chat` — confirm the board tools (`kilo_board_read`, `kilo_board_write`) are registered (check `ax chat --help` or the tool list). Also test the umbrella flag (`KILO_EXPERIMENTAL=1`) and verify it works the same way. Touches src/tool/tools/board.ts, possibly src/config/index.ts.

#### 3. Kilocode #14012, #14005: performance optimizations — defer diff parsing and lightweight todo checkbox (LOW priority, performance)

- **What**: Two Kilocode VS Code UI performance fixes: (1) #14012 defers diff parsing until tool cards expand (collapsed tools no longer parse their diff bodies on mount), (2) #14005 renders read-only todo checkboxes without Kobalte (Solid.js component library), reducing component overhead. Both are desktop-app-specific rendering optimizations.
- **Why**: Large diffs (e.g. multi-file patches, bulk refactors) slow down transcript rendering when every collapsed tool card parses its body on mount. Deferring the parse until the user expands the card reduces initial render time. Similarly, Kobalte's checkbox component is heavier than a plain HTML checkbox for read-only displays (todo items in the transcript), so dropping it speeds up todo-heavy transcripts.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14012 (perf(ui): defer diff parsing until tool cards expand), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14005 (perf(ui): render read-only todo checkbox without Kobalte)
- **Category**: command (VS Code UI, performance)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no VS Code extension, no Solid.js UI, no Kobalte components. This is Kilocode desktop-specific. Not CLI-portable.

#### 4. Cline #14025: PowerShell edition identification — shell edition export Node-only (LOW priority, Cline internal API)

- **What**: Cline's PowerShell edition identification helper (which distinguishes PowerShell 5.1 from PowerShell 7+) is now exported from `@cline/shared`, but only on the Node surface (not browser). This is a follow-up to #13815 (nested PowerShell script preservation, analyzed in 2026-09-10), exposing the edition-detection logic so other modules can use it without duplicating the probing code.
- **Why**: Edition detection (5.1 vs 7+) is needed by the nested-script unwrapper (#13815) and potentially by other shell-related features (e.g. script compatibility warnings, edition-specific flags). Keeping it in one place reduces drift. The browser export was removed because it is meaningless outside Node (no filesystem, no shell probing).
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14025 (fix(core): identify shell editions and discourage redundant wrappers)
- **Category**: tool (bash, PowerShell, internal API)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. This is Cline's internal API refactor, not a new user-facing feature. Alexi's PowerShell handling (src/tool/tools/bash.ts, src/tool/tools/shell/id.ts) already detects editions (pwsh.exe = 7+, powershell.exe = 5.1) and prioritizes pwsh. The 2026-09-10 recommendation for #13815 (nested PowerShell script preservation) is still open — port the unwrapping logic, not the edition export. Not actionable today.

#### 5. Cline #13837: unified Customize tab styling — Tools/Skills/Rules/Workflows toggle switches (LOW priority, Cline desktop UI)

- **What**: Cline desktop app's Customize view now uses a consistent list style across Tools, Skills, Rules, and Workflows tabs: section titles with counts (`BuiltIn Tools <count>`), toggle switches to enable/disable items in place, search bars, Enable all / Disable all checkboxes per section, and dots menus (Copy path / Uninstall) for Skills and Rules. Skills gained a toggle switch (previously had only an Uninstall button), and disabled skills are no longer filtered out of the listing so they can be found and re-enabled. Workflows and Rules show disabled toggle switches (not yet wired up in the backend). The tabs are reordered to Tools, Plugins, Skills, Rules, MCP, Hooks and default to the Tools tab.
- **Why**: The four tabs had inconsistent UI patterns (separate controls, different enable/disable flows, some hiding disabled items). Unifying them makes the desktop app's configuration surface more learnable and reduces visual noise. Skills can now be disabled without being uninstalled, matching how Plugins work.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13837 (Unify Tools, Skills, and Rules tab styling in desktop Customize view)
- **Category**: command (Cline desktop UI, configuration)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi has no desktop Customize view, no electron app. This is Cline desktop-specific. Not CLI-portable.

#### 6. Cline #14003: refresh live model catalogs for all shared providers — fix catalog refresh scope (LOW priority, Cline provider architecture)

- **What**: Cline desktop app now refreshes live model catalogs for ALL shared providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.), not just the currently selected one. Previously only the active provider's catalog was refreshed on startup, so switching providers mid-session could show stale model lists. The fix excludes private catalogs (e.g. custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints) from the bulk refresh and measures model load telemetry.
- **Why**: Stale model catalogs caused users to see outdated model lists (missing new models, listing deprecated models) after switching providers. Refreshing all shared providers on startup ensures the catalogs are fresh before the first turn. Private/custom providers are excluded because they may have auth requirements or non-standard endpoints that should not be probed automatically.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14003 (fix(desktop): refresh live model catalogs for all shared providers)
- **Category**: provider (model catalog, Cline)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP. Alexi uses a single-provider architecture (SAP AI Core Orchestration) with one live model catalog refresh on startup (src/providers/modelCatalog.ts, `refreshModelCatalog`). There are no multiple shared providers to refresh, so this pattern does not apply. Not actionable.
